title: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M on gfx1151: the sampled MTP route publishes the same tokens as the autoregressive route for forced-token queues, output constraints, and thinking budgets
purpose: Forced tokens, force-sequence completion, json_object_close_forcing, tool_call_constraint, and a thinking budget are caller-level overrides: the autoregressive route emits the queued head instead of drawing, masks a row from the decoded text of the tokens before it, queues a closing suffix when the remaining budget is exactly enough to close the structure, and turns a reached thinking cap into a queued close sequence. This records that the speculative route does the same. Both arms run the same requests through hipengine.LLM, so the route is the only difference. No speed claim is made or implied.

coverage.covered: Eight requests on both arms: a three-token queue, a four-token queue longer than one verified chain, the same queue on the sampled branch (temperature 0.7), a json_object request whose object closes at its budget, a required tool_call_constraint whose envelope closes at its budget, a thinking budget whose hard cap queues its close sequence mid-cycle at temperature 0.7 and again at temperature 0.0, and a force-sequence completion whose first token is the case prompt's own first token (taken from an unforced probe of that prompt). An unforced request runs before and after the forced ones on both arms.
coverage.not_covered: The thinking cases exercise the hard cap; the soft-close window (its positive logit bias on the first close token) is not exercised. Multi-choice (n>1) requests are task 17. The tool case uses mode=required so the tool branch is forced; an auto-mode request that takes its plain-text branch is not exercised here.

acceptance.queue_isolated: The unforced request run after every forced case published the same ids as the unforced seed request on the speculative arm, and the same ids as the autoregressive arm.
acceptance.force_sequence_completion: The model's own seed token plus the two queued tokens were published as [16570, 81099, 12102] on both arms, so the remainder was queued and emitted from inside the cycle.
acceptance.forced_prefix_published: Every forced case published its queued tokens at the head of the output, in order, on both arms.
acceptance.continuation_parity: Every greedy case published the autoregressive arm's exact ids (6 cases), so the queue was consumed exactly once and the continuation was not disturbed. The two sampled cases published the forced prefix on both arms; their continuations are different draws from the same law because the accept walk consumes the request's uniform stream per verified row.
acceptance.route_ran: Every speculative case reported gguf_specdec2_mtp2 while every autoregressive case reported a plain decode path.
acceptance.tool_call_envelope: The required tool case published one complete canonical envelope on both arms, byte-identical: <tool_call>{"name":"read","arguments":{"path":"/tmp/notes.txt"}}</tool_call>. The constraint admits only that envelope in this mode, so the branch, the per-row mask, and the forced closing suffix are all load-bearing.
acceptance.thinking_close_at_the_cap: Both thinking cases queued a 4-token close sequence at a cap of 8 reasoning tokens, and both arms published that sequence starting at index 8 -- the MTP arm through speculative cycles, the autoregressive arm step by step -- so the cap's position is the same on both routes and does not depend on the draw. The close sequence is the budget's own token ids, and the answer phase follows it.

observation.queue_consumed_across_cycles: The two-token case ran 10 cycles for 23 speculative output tokens, and the three-token case ran 18 cycles for 31: the queue outlives a single cycle and is consumed one published position at a time.
observation.sampled_branch: The sampled case ran 15 cycles and published the forced prefix identically on both arms. Its continuation is a different draw from the same law, which is the documented behavior of the sampled route: the accept walk draws one uniform per verified row where the autoregressive route draws one per step.
observation.force_sequence_trigger: The force-sequence case queued [16570, 81099, 12102] where the first element is the case prompt's own first token from an unforced probe, so the partial match is guaranteed to trigger on the token the model emits anyway; both arms published exactly that sequence.
observation.route_confirmed: Every speculative case reported execution_path=gguf_specdec2_mtp2 and every autoregressive case reported a plain decode path, so no comparison is between two autoregressive runs.
observation.defect_found_and_fixed: The first live run of this gate caught an UnboundLocalError in the host sampled-accept path (a function-local import of the row walk shadowing the module import), which the engine contained by falling back to autoregressive decoding for that request. Fixed, and pinned by tests/test_unit_mtp_native_sampling.py test_host_sampled_accept_resolves_forced_overrides_without_consuming_them.
observation.declared_context_honored: Both arms constructed their engine with max_sequence_length=4096 and no prepare() call, and both resident sessions were sized to 4096 rather than to automatic selection. That is the default configuration: no HIPENGINE_GGUF_AUTO_CONTEXT override is set.
observation.json_object_close: The json_object case published a closed object at exactly its 12-token budget and published the autoregressive arm's ids token for token (5 cycles, 10 speculative tokens). The constraint's closing suffix is what closes the object at the budget, and the autoregressive arm runs the same rule.
observation.tool_branch_live: The tool case ran 6 speculative cycles at depth 3 for 18 MTP-published tokens plus one AR step, and both arms published the same 20 ids. It failed the first time it ran, and both defects it exposed were in the route rather than in the constraint: sampled_accept_summary dropped the text observer the adapter handed it, so a cycle's later rows were masked against a DFA that had not seen the earlier tokens, and the route published a newline inside the envelope. A row advanced by such a violating draft token has no admissible law; it is unreachable, because the row before it is masked against the same DFA and excludes that token, so the walk records it as invalid rather than raising and the accept walk refuses to step onto it.
observation.thinking_budget_live: The thinking budget needed one wiring fix and one real defect fixed. The walk now prepares each row's selection exactly where the autoregressive route does, which is what turns a reached hard cap into a queued close sequence; before that, the walk reported no override for the row the cap governs. The defect was in the commit: it consumed overrides as a leading prefix of the published chain, which holds for a request's own forced queue (emitted first) but not for a cap reached mid-cycle. A cycle that published the close at position 2 of 3 popped a position that had no override and raised. The commit now consumes exactly the positions the walk reported, so a non-leading override is handled the same way. A second case runs the same cap at temperature 0.0, where there is no draw to hide a difference behind: both arms published all 24 ids identically with the close at index 8, and the MTP arm reached it through 9 cycles.
observation.greedy_thinking_parity: The greedy thinking case is the cap's strongest check: with temperature 0.0 the two arms must publish the same ids token for token, so the close position, the close sequence, and the answer that follows it are all compared rather than only the index the close starts at.
